samples.text:
The graph shows the number of international visitors who travelled to Spain, Thailand and Mexico between 2015 and 2023.

Spain had the most visitors in most years. In 2015 there were 68 million visitors and this increased every year to 84 million in 2019. Thailand and Mexico had much less visitors, about 30 million in 2015, and both of them increased slowly to 40 and 45 million in 2019.

In 2020 there was a big fall in all countries. Spain dropped to only 19 million and Thailand to 7 million. Mexico also fell to 24 million but it was the highest country in this year. In 2021 Thailand got almost no visitor, only 0.4 million, while Mexico went back to 32 million.

After 2021 the number of visitors increased again. In 2023 Spain had 85 million, it was more than in 2019. Mexico had 42 million, but Thailand only had 28 million.

Overall, the three countries had similar trends, they increased, then fell in 2020 and after that recovered, but Thailand recover slowly.
samples.why: Overview present but late and simplistic · key features, including the 2020 collapse, covered · adequate but repetitive vocabulary · comma splices, a 'less/fewer' error and a verb form error.

samples.text:
The line graph compares the number of international tourists arriving in Spain, Thailand and Mexico each year from 2015 to 2023.

Overall, arrivals in all three countries grew steadily until 2019, collapsed in 2020 and then recovered. Spain was the most popular destination in most years, but the extent of the recovery varied considerably, with Thailand recovering the slowest.

Between 2015 and 2019, visitor numbers to Spain rose from 68 million to 84 million, while Mexico and Thailand, which started at similar levels, increased to 45 million and 40 million respectively. In 2020, however, all three experienced a dramatic decline. Spain's arrivals fell to 19 million, less than a quarter of the previous year, and Thailand's dropped to 7 million. Mexico was affected the least, with 24 million visitors, making it the most visited of the three countries that year.

In 2021, Thailand's figure fell even further to just 0.4 million, whereas Mexico had already returned to 32 million. By 2023, Spain had fully recovered, with 85 million arrivals, surpassing its 2019 level. Mexico's figure was 42 million, slightly below than its pre-2020 peak, while Thailand attracted only 28 million visitors.
samples.why: Clear overview of growth, collapse and uneven recovery · key features highlighted · logical progression · good range of cohesive devices · accurate derived comparisons · generally accurate with a minor slip.

samples.text:
The graph presents annual international visitor arrivals in Spain, Thailand and Mexico between 2015 and 2023.

The three countries followed a broadly similar trajectory, with steady growth to 2019, a sudden collapse in 2020 and a subsequent recovery. However, the scale of both the downturn and the rebound differed markedly: Spain regained and slightly exceeded its former level, whereas Thailand was still well short of it in 2023.

Spain was consistently the leading destination apart from the disrupted years. Its arrivals climbed from 68 million in 2015 to 84 million in 2019, while Mexico and Thailand, both starting at around 30 million, reached 45 million and 40 million respectively.

The drop in 2020 was severe for Spain and Thailand, whose figures plummeted to 19 million and 7 million. Mexico proved far more resilient, falling only to 24 million and, in 2021, briefly overtaking Spain with 32 million arrivals against 31 million. Thailand, meanwhile, sank further to a negligible 0.4 million that year. The recovery thereafter was rapid for Spain, which reached a peak of 85 million by 2023, and fairly solid for Mexico, at 42 million, but Thailand's 28 million remained around 70% of its 2019 total.
samples.why: Skilful selection of key features, including Mexico's brief lead · clear overview · accurate figures and derived comparisons · precise vocabulary such as 'resilient' · wide range of error-free structures.
